disclaimer: Guides are starting points, not recipes. Air fryers vary by brand, wattage and basket size — always check early and verify meat, poultry and fish with an instant-read thermometer.
trust: Every number here is calculated from fixed data tables — USDA safe minimum internal temperatures, our own 54 tested charts, and manufacturer guidebooks. No AI, no guessing: the same food and settings always produce the same guide.

fresh.label: Fresh or fully thawed
fresh.q: What state is the food in?

frozen.label: Frozen — straight from the freezer
frozen.note: Cooking from frozen: no thawing needed, expect roughly 50% more time. If the package gives instructions, follow them.

marinated.label: Marinated
marinated.note: Marinade adds surface moisture — about 10% more time, and always pat the pieces dry before they go in (wet surfaces steam instead of brown).

breaded.label: Breaded / crumbed
breaded.note: Breadcrumbs brown faster than naked meat — 5°F lower, a touch longer, and one light oil spray at the start for even color.

reheat.label: Leftover — reheating
reheat.note: USDA rule for leftovers: reheat until the food steams and reaches 165°F / 74°C all the way through.

thawed_only.label: Thawed (never cook this one frozen)
thawed_only.note: This one must be thawed first — frozen pieces finish outside long before the center is safe.

crispy.label: Maximum crisp
crispy.note: Crisp mode: 15°F hotter, about 10% less time — single layer is what actually makes it crisp.

quick.label: As fast as possible
quick.note: Quick mode: hotter and shorter — start checking at the low end.

juicy.label: Juicy and tender
juicy.note: Juicy mode: gentler heat, a little longer - still verify the full safe internal temperature before resting.

protein: Pat the food dry with paper towels — dry surfaces brown, wet ones steam.
Preheat the air fryer {preheat_note} to {temp}°F / {temp_c}°C (3 minutes).
Arrange in a single layer with air space between pieces. Light oil spray if you want deeper color.
Check early at {early} min. Verify with an instant-read thermometer: {internal}°F / {internal_c}°C in the thickest piece.
veg: Cut into even pieces — uniform size is what makes vegetables finish together.
Toss with 1–2 tsp oil, salt, and any seasoning; shake off excess.
Preheat the air fryer {preheat_note} to {temp}°F / {temp_c}°C (3 minutes).
Air fry in a single layer at {temp}°F for {tmin}–{tmax} minutes, shaking the basket halfway.
Done when {check}. Taste and adjust salt while hot.
frozen_snack: No thawing, no preheat needed — frozen straight into the basket.
Pour in a single layer; do not overcrowd (cook in batches for extra crisp).
Air fry at {temp}°F / {temp_c}°C for {tmin}–{tmax} minutes, shaking halfway.
Done when {check}. Serve immediately — they crisp, then soften as they cool.
baked: Line the basket with parchment (with airflow holes) if the dough is soft or sticky.
Preheat the air fryer {preheat_note} to {temp}°F / {temp_c}°C (3 minutes).
Air fry at {temp}°F for {tmin}–{tmax} minutes until {check}.
Check one piece first — every dough brand bakes differently. Adjust in 1-minute steps.
reheat_tpl: Let the food sit out 2–3 minutes while the air fryer preheats to {temp}°F / {temp_c}°C.
Arrange in a single layer — overlap makes soggy spots.
Air fry {tmin}–{tmax} minutes until steaming hot all the way through (165°F / 74°C for anything with meat).
Check the center of the thickest piece, not just the edges.

foods.name: Chicken breast (boneless)
foods.check: juices run clear and the center is white, not pink
tips: Even thickness = even cooking. Pound thick ends to about 1 inch.
Safe at 165°F — juicier if you pull it at 160-162°F and let carryover finish it.
Brined 30 minutes in salt water stays noticeably juicier.

foods.name: Chicken thighs (boneless)
foods.check: browned outside, 165°F inside — thighs stay juicy even past 175°F
tips: Thighs are forgiving: 175°F gives the best texture and is still safe.

foods.name: Chicken thighs (bone-in)
foods.check: meat pulls back from the bone and reads 165°F

foods.name: Chicken drumsticks
foods.check: meat shrinks from the drum tip and reads 165°F
tips: Flip at the midpoint — the skin side needs both rounds of heat.

foods.name: Chicken wings (whole)
foods.check: skin is crisp and blistered, 165°F at the bone
tips: Toss with 1 tsp baking powder (not soda) + salt for shatter-crisp skin.
Sauce AFTER cooking, not before — wet wings never crisp.

foods.name: Chicken tenders / strips
foods.check: golden crust, white center at 165°F

foods.name: Whole small chicken (3–5 lb)
foods.check: 165°F in the thigh (not touching bone) and clear juices
tips: Spatchcocked (backbone removed) chicken cooks far more evenly in a basket.
steps: Pat the bird very dry inside and out; rub with oil and salt generously.
Truss tight and tuck the wings so they do not scorch.
Preheat to 360°F / 182°C. Breast-side DOWN for the first half keeps the breast juicy.
Air fry 360°F for the computed time, flipping breast-up at the midpoint.
Verify 165°F in the thickest thigh. Rest 10 minutes before carving.

foods.name: Turkey breast cutlets
foods.check: white throughout, 165°F center
tips: Turkey dries out fast — check at the low end of the range.

foods.name: Ground chicken / turkey burgers
foods.check: no pink anywhere, 165°F center — poultry burgers dry out fast
tips: A spoon of olive oil or grated onion in the mix fights dryness.

foods.name: Homemade chicken nuggets
foods.check: golden crust, 165°F center
tips: One oil spray on the breaded side before cooking = noticeably crisper.

foods.name: Steak (sirloin, ribeye, NY strip)
foods.check: 145°F is the USDA safe minimum (medium) — rest 5 min
tips: Check in the thickest piece - the 3-minute rest is part of the USDA standard, not optional.
Preference guide (not the safety line): 130-135°F medium-rare, 145°F medium, 160°F well.
Preheated basket + dry surface = the crust you want.

foods.name: Beef burgers
foods.check: no pink for safety — 160°F for ground beef per USDA
tips: Dimple the patty center — it stops the burger from ballooning.
Cheese in the last 30 seconds, lid closed or foil tent.

foods.name: Meatballs (1 oz)
foods.check: browned outside, 160°F center
tips: Roll same-size balls — mixed sizes never finish together.
Sauce after, or the coating goes soggy.

foods.name: Beef cubes / kabobs (1.5")
foods.check: 145°F for whole-muscle cubes (USDA medium)
tips: Skewers: soak wooden ones 20 min, snap to basket length.

foods.name: Small beef roast (2–3 lb)
foods.check: 145°F center — rest 10 min, it will rise a few degrees
steps: Tie or shape the roast into an even cylinder; rub oil, salt, pepper.
Preheat to 375°F / 190°C.
Air fry 40-55 min depending on size, flipping once.
Start checking at 35 min: 145°F center (USDA safe minimum).
Rest 10 min under foil — carryover finishes it.

foods.name: Mini meatloaves
foods.check: 160°F center — glaze in the last 5 minutes

foods.name: Salisbury patties with gravy
foods.check: 160°F center; warm the gravy separately on the stove

foods.name: Hot dogs / sausages (pre-cooked)
foods.check: steaming hot with browned, snappy casing — they are pre-cooked, so this is about texture
tips: Score diagonal slits so they do not split and curl.
Buns: 1 minute, cut-side up, after the dogs.

foods.name: Pork chops (1 inch)
foods.check: 145°F with a blush of pink is safe and juicy per USDA
tips: The old 'no pink pork' rule is outdated — 145°F + 3 min rest is the USDA standard.
Brine 30 min in 5% salt water for a guaranteed juicy chop.

foods.name: Pork tenderloin (whole)
foods.check: 145°F center — it is a lean muscle, do not overcook it
tips: Silver skin removed; two tenderloins fit most baskets side by side.

foods.name: Pork medallions (2 inch)
foods.check: 145°F center

foods.name: Pork belly slices
foods.check: fat edges are crisp and glassy, meat reads 145°F+
tips: Score the fat in a crosshatch so it renders instead of curling.
Drain the basket halfway — rendered fat smokes above 400°F.

foods.name: Fresh sausage links
foods.check: firm to the touch, 160°F center, no pink
tips: Do not pierce — the juices ARE the flavor.

foods.name: Bacon (regular cut)
foods.check: crisp and evenly mahogany — it keeps crisping on the rack as it cools
tips: A splash of water in the drawer catches grease smoke.
Thick-cut: use the Thick Bacon entry.
steps: Lay strips in a single layer; overlap turns to rubber.
No preheat needed — start cold-ish for even render.
Air fry 360°F / 182°C for the computed time. No flip required.
Drain the drawer grease before the NEXT batch — hot fat in the drawer smokes.
Rest on a rack, not paper towels — towels steam the bottom.

foods.name: Bacon (thick cut)
foods.check: crisp but still bendy if you like it chewy — lower temp renders thick fat without burning

foods.name: Ham slices (fully cooked)
foods.check: 140°F throughout (USDA for reheated cooked ham) — glazed edges caramelize
tips: Score the fat edge so slices lie flat and do not curl.

foods.name: Country-style ribs
foods.check: safe at 145°F — fall-apart tender happens closer to 195°F, your call
tips: Fork-tender, not just safe: add time in 5-minute steps past 145°F.
Sauce only in the last 5 minutes — sugar burns.

foods.name: Spare / baby back ribs (half rack)
foods.check: bones twist free when truly done; 145°F is the safety floor
steps: Remove the membrane on the bone side; rub with dry spice.
Preheat to 360°F / 182°C.
Air fry 30-40 min meat-side up, then flip for the last 10.
Sauce for the final 5 minutes only.
Safe at 145°F; restaurant-tender is ~190-200°F — keep going in 5-min steps if you want it falling apart.

foods.name: Lamb chops (1 inch)
foods.check: 145°F USDA minimum — rest 5 min for the juices to settle
tips: Trim excess fat cap — it smokes hard in a 400°F basket.

foods.name: Lamb kofta / kebabs
foods.check: 160°F center (ground lamb), browned outside
tips: Skewer length must clear the element — cut wooden skewers to fit.

foods.name: Leg of lamb cubes
foods.check: 145°F for whole-muscle cubes

foods.name: Salmon fillet
foods.check: flakes at the thickest point but still translucent-orange in the very center — 145°F
tips: Skin-side down the whole way; the skin shields the flesh and crisps nicely.
A pinch of sugar in the seasoning speeds up surface caramelization.

foods.name: Cod / haddock / white fish
foods.check: opaque and flaking — white fish goes from perfect to dry in one minute
tips: White fish is lean: check at the LOW end of the range.

foods.name: Tilapia fillet
foods.check: opaque, flakes easily, 145°F

foods.name: Shrimp (large, peeled)
foods.check: C-shaped and opaque — straight = undercooked, tight O = overcooked
tips: Shrimp moves at the speed of the range: start checking at 4 minutes.

foods.name: Sea scallops
foods.check: opaque center with a golden top — milky center means undercooked
tips: Pat VERY dry; a wet scallop steams and never browns.

foods.name: Tuna steak
foods.check: USDA safe minimum is 145°F (well-done fish). Rare tuna is a preference some cooks make — the thermometer decides, not the clock.
tips: Frozen sashimi-grade tuna thaws fast — 20 min in cool water.

foods.name: Crab cakes
foods.check: golden crust, 145°F center, springs back
tips: Chill formed cakes 20 min — they hold shape instead of slumping.

foods.name: Lobster tail
foods.check: meat is opaque white, shell bright red — 145°F
tips: Butterfly the shell (kitchen shears) so the meat sits flat and soaks up butter.

foods.name: Calamari rings (frozen, breaded)
foods.check: deep golden and crisp — a minute too long turns them rubbery

foods.name: French fries (frozen)
foods.check: deep golden, crisp outside, fluffy inside
tips: Shake every 5 minutes — frozen fries clump fast.
Cook in two smaller batches rather than one crowded one.

foods.name: Curly fries (frozen)
foods.check: seasoning darkened, edges crisp

foods.name: Waffle fries (frozen)
foods.check: golden with crisp lattice edges

foods.name: Sweet potato fries (frozen)
foods.check: caramelized edges — sugars burn fast, shake twice
tips: Sweet potato sugars brown quicker than potato — check 2 minutes early.

foods.name: Tater tots (frozen)
foods.check: deep gold all over, crunchy shell
tips: Single layer, and DO shake — the centers stay soggy where tots touch.

foods.name: Hash brown patties (frozen)
foods.check: crisp golden crust both sides — flip at midpoint

foods.name: Mozzarella sticks (frozen)
foods.check: breading golden, cheese JUST starting to peek — one minute late equals a blowout
tips: Check at 5 minutes. A burst stick means the batch is already done.
Freeze again 10 min if thawed — cold sticks hold their cheese.

foods.name: Pizza rolls (frozen)
foods.check: blistered golden — the filling is molten lava, rest 2 min
tips: They hold heat like little volcanoes — bite after a 2-minute rest.
Overlapping rolls steam instead of crisping — spread them.

foods.name: Bagel bites (frozen)
foods.check: cheese bubbling, bottoms crisp — put shiny side up per package

foods.name: Corn dogs (frozen)
foods.check: batter golden and firm, hot center
tips: Stand them upright against the basket wall if they fit — or lay flat and flip.

foods.name: Mini corn dogs (frozen)
foods.check: golden batter, hot center

foods.name: Onion rings (frozen)
foods.check: crisp and dark gold — rings go from crisp to burnt in 2 minutes
tips: Spread wide; stacked rings steam and go limp.

foods.name: Jalapeño poppers (frozen)
foods.check: crust golden, filling molten — cream cheese stays nuclear-hot, rest 2 min

foods.name: Spring / egg rolls (frozen)
foods.check: wrapper blistered and crisp, filling steaming
tips: Flip once — the seam side down first, then crisp the top.

foods.name: Samosas (frozen)
foods.check: crisp pastry, steaming center — thick folds need the full range

foods.name: Empanadas (frozen)
foods.check: golden crimped edge, hot filling — rest 2 min

foods.name: Taquitos / flautas (frozen)
foods.check: shell rigid and crisp, filling steaming

foods.name: Dumplings / potstickers (frozen)
foods.check: bottoms browned, wrappers translucent-steamed
steps: Brush or spray the bottoms with oil — this makes the crispy side.
Frozen straight in, flat-side down, no preheat.
Air fry 380°F / 193°C for 9-13 min. Shake gently halfway.
For soup-style: finish with a 1-tbsp water sprinkle in the last 2 min and tent with foil.

foods.name: Fish sticks (frozen)
foods.check: crust crisp and golden, fish flaking hot

foods.name: Breaded fish fillets (frozen)
foods.check: crust crisp, fish steaming and flaky inside

foods.name: Chicken nuggets (frozen)
foods.check: evenly golden, hot center — nuggets vary by brand, trust the color
tips: Shake once at 5 min for even gold on both faces.

foods.name: Breaded chicken strips (frozen)
foods.check: deep golden crust, chicken steaming inside

foods.name: Chicken patties (frozen)
foods.check: crisp edges, hot center — patties hold heat, rest 2 min

foods.name: Mac & cheese bites (frozen)
foods.check: crust set and golden — the center is molten cheese, rest before biting

foods.name: Veggie burgers (frozen)
foods.check: brown crust both sides, steaming center — flip carefully, they are delicate

foods.name: Broccoli florets
foods.check: tips charred at the edges, stem fork-tender
tips: Cut stems thick — they are the best part when caramelized.
Underfill oil: 1 tsp is enough; pools of oil make smoke.

foods.name: Cauliflower florets
foods.check: deep gold spots, tender core

foods.name: Brussels sprouts (halved)
foods.check: outer leaves crisp and dark, center pierced easily
tips: Cut-side down the whole way — that flat face is where the candy happens.
Halve, don't quarter — quarters burn their leaves first.

foods.name: Carrots (thick coins or batons)
foods.check: edges caramelized, center fork-tender

foods.name: Baby carrots
foods.check: blistered and tender — smaller ones finish 2 minutes early

foods.name: Asparagus
foods.check: bright green with charred tips, still snappy-tender
tips: Asparagus races: 1 minute past perfect turns it to string.

foods.name: Green beans
foods.check: wrinkled, blistered, tender-crisp

foods.name: Zucchini (half-moons)
foods.check: brown edges, still slightly bouncy — squash collapses fast
tips: Salt and drain 10 min first if you hate sogginess.

foods.name: Bell pepper strips
foods.check: soft with blackened blister spots

foods.name: Mushrooms (halved)
foods.check: shrunken, deep brown, juices reabsorbed
tips: No oil needed — they release their own and crisp in it.

foods.name: Eggplant cubes
foods.check: creamy center, browned edges — salt cubes 15 min and dry first

foods.name: Okra (whole or halved)
foods.check: edges crisp, slime gone — high dry heat is the anti-slime trick

foods.name: Corn on the cob
foods.check: kernels plump with roasted brown spots
tips: Husk on works too: add 3 min and cut the silk off after.

foods.name: Cherry tomatoes
foods.check: skins blistered and split — they turn jammy as they cool

foods.name: Butternut squash cubes
foods.check: caramelized edges, fork slides through

foods.name: Parsnips (batons)
foods.check: golden and tender — sweeter than carrots when roasted hard

foods.name: Beets (1-inch cubes)
foods.check: shriveled edges, fork-tender center

foods.name: Cabbage wedges
foods.check: charred leaves outside, silky heart inside

foods.name: Baked potato (russet)
foods.check: fork slides to the center with no resistance, skin crackled
tips: Pierce 6-8 times with a fork — unvented potatoes can split hard.
Oil + salt the skin before: that IS the crackle.
For crispier skin, finish 5 min at 425°F.

foods.name: Potato wedges (fresh)
foods.check: crust golden and stiff, center fluffy
tips: Soak cut wedges in cold water 20 min, dry VERY well, then toss with oil and cornstarch — that is the crunch formula.

foods.name: Baked sweet potato
foods.check: skin puckered, syrup leaking, fork slides through
tips: The syrup bubbling out is the sign of a perfect one — catch it before it burns.

foods.name: Sweet potato cubes
foods.check: caramelized on edges, soft center — sugars scorch fast, shake twice

foods.name: Baby potatoes (halved)
foods.check: cut faces golden, center tender
tips: Microwave 3 min first for a head start, then 10-12 min air fry for the crust.

foods.name: Potato skins
foods.check: shell crisp, cheese molten — pre-baked potato halves, scooped and filled
steps: Start with baked potato halves (see Baked potato), scoop to ¼ inch shell.
Brush with oil, air fry 400°F 5 min to crisp the shell alone.
Fill with cheese/bacon, air fry 4-7 min more until molten.

foods.name: Breakfast sausage links (pre-cooked)
foods.check: browned casing, steaming center — pre-cooked, so this is color and heat

foods.name: Breakfast sausage patties (fresh)
foods.check: no pink, 160°F center — ground meat rule
tips: Dimple the center like a burger to keep them flat.

foods.name: Eggs (sunny side, ramekin)
foods.check: white fully set, yolk still liquid — butter the ramekin well
steps: Butter or spray a ramekin; crack the egg in.
Air fry 350°F / 177°C. 4-5 min runny yolk, 6-7 min set yolk.
Season after — salt raw yolk draws moisture.

foods.name: Eggs (hard-boiled)
foods.check: yolk set with no green ring — 250°F is correct, low and slow
tips: Room-temp eggs crack less in the hot basket.
steps: Place whole uncracked eggs in the basket — no water needed.
Air fry 250°F / 121°C for 15-17 min.
Straight into ice water for 5 min — this stops the green ring AND makes peeling easy.

foods.name: Scrambled eggs (ramekin)
foods.check: just set and glossy — they keep cooking in the hot ramekin, pull early
steps: Beat eggs with a splash of cream; pour into a buttered ramekin.
Air fry 350°F, stir once at half-time with a fork.
They firm up as they rest — slightly loose is correct.

foods.name: Shredded hash browns (fresh patty)
foods.check: lattice crust brown and rigid
tips: Squeeze the shreds bone-dry in a towel — water is the enemy of crisp.

foods.name: French toast sticks
foods.check: golden crust, custard just set — bread brands differ, check one early

foods.name: Canned biscuits
foods.check: deep gold top, hollow knock on the bottom
tips: Every can brand bakes differently — sacrifice one biscuit to calibrate.

foods.name: Canned cinnamon rolls
foods.check: puffed and golden, center roll still slightly soft
tips: Icing AFTER — heat melts it into the spiral.

foods.name: Crescent rolls (canned)
foods.check: golden, puffed, no doughy seams

foods.name: Cookie dough (portioned)
foods.check: edges golden, centers still soft — they set as they cool
tips: Parchment with holes, or a tiny rack — flat bottoms need airflow.
2 inches of spacing or they merge into one mega-cookie.

foods.name: Garlic bread (frozen)
foods.check: butter bubbling, edges gold — cheese-top versions need the extra minute

foods.name: Garlic bread (fresh baguette)
foods.check: crisp edges, butter absorbed

foods.name: Frozen pizza (personal)
foods.check: cheese fully melted and spotted, crust bottom firm
steps: Straight from freezer to basket — box instructions for ovens run hotter than air fryers need.
370°F / 188°C for 11-16 min depending on size. Rotate once.
Slide a spatula under early to check the bottom — dark = done.

foods.name: Soft pretzels (frozen)
foods.check: puffed, salt shining — brush with butter after

foods.name: Churros (frozen)
foods.check: crisp shell, hot center — sugar-coat while hot

foods.name: Naan / pita (warming)
foods.check: puffed slightly, pliable with warm spots — seconds matter, stay at the oven

foods.name: Hand pies (frozen)
foods.check: crust golden and crisp, filling steaming — vent warning: molten fruit burns

foods.name: Pizza slice (leftover)
foods.check: cheese re-melted, crust bottom firm — reheat until steaming (165°F rule for meat toppings)
tips: One drop of water in the basket corner + foil tent = revived melty cheese.

foods.name: Fried chicken (leftover)
foods.check: steaming through to the bone — 165°F in the thickest piece (USDA leftover rule)
tips: 360°F, not 400 — high heat burns the crust before the center thaws.

foods.name: Fries (leftover)
foods.check: crisp outside, hot center — they never return to fresh, but close
tips: Skip the oil — leftover fries carry their own.

foods.name: Steak (leftover, sliced)
foods.check: warm through — reheat to 165°F per USDA, but fast and low keeps it pink-ish
tips: 350°F only: leftover steak overcooks in seconds.
A pat of butter on top while reheating restores the gloss.

foods.name: Mac & cheese (baked portion)
foods.check: bubbling at the edges, steaming center (165°F rule)
tips: Foil cover for the first half, crisp uncovered for the last half.

foods.name: Casserole portion
foods.check: steaming center — thick casseroles hide cold spots, test the middle

foods.name: Roasted vegetables (leftover)
foods.check: re-crisped edges, hot through

foods.name: Spring rolls (leftover)
foods.check: wrapper re-crisped, filling steaming

foods.name: Baked apples (whole)
foods.check: knife slides in like butter, skin wrinkled
tips: Core but leave the base intact — a fruit boat, not a leak.
Cinnamon-sugar in the core melts INTO the apple.

foods.name: Caramelized banana halves
foods.check: golden-brown faces, edges melting — slightly firm center is best

foods.name: Pineapple rings
foods.check: brown spots, edges curling — sugars concentrate

foods.name: Peach halves
foods.check: soft at the pit, caramelized rim — serve with the juices

foods.name: Leftover brownie (rewarm)
foods.check: gooey-warm center — 300°F only, it burns fast
tips: The ice-cream-on-top rule applies. Obviously.

foods.name: Tofu (crispy cubes)
foods.check: deep gold, spongy-crisp shell — press the block 15 min first
tips: Press between towels 15 min, toss with 1 tsp cornstarch: the crisp formula.
Cornstarch, not flour — flour goes gummy.
Sauce after cooking, never before.

foods.name: Roasted chickpeas
foods.check: they rattle dry in the basket — any soft rattle means more time
tips: Pat them bone-dry first; wet chickpeas steam.
Season AFTER — salt on wet skins draws moisture and softens them.

foods.name: Halloumi slices
foods.check: golden grill marks, squeaky-soft center — it holds shape, no flipping stress

foods.name: Grilled cheese sandwich
foods.check: bread golden, cheese fully runny when lifted
steps: Butter the OUTSIDE of both slices; cheese inside.
Air fry 370°F / 188°C for 5-7 min, flip carefully at midpoint.
Toothpick through the corner keeps the top slice from flying to the element.

foods.name: Quesadilla
foods.check: tortilla crisp-spotted, cheese molten — fold under a weight after

foods.name: Falafel (frozen)
foods.check: crust firm and browned, interior steaming — flip gently
